messages:
mike.carter: FYI found a batch of legacy snapshots uploaded with SSE-S3 and missing retention tags during the compliance spot-check. Some date back to 2022.
jordan.lee: how many? are they in one bucket or spread?
mike.carter: ~3200 objects across two buckets. One bucket had SSE-KMS with an old org CMK, the other bucket showed SSE-S3 objects plus a few with `retention: none` tag.
sarah.nelson: risk: SSE-S3 objects are not tied to our CMK policies. If a bucket policy accidentally allowed reads, potential data exposure. We should treat as potential vuln.
leo: root cause hypothesis: uploader agent pre-2023 didn't set retention tags or KMS headers. We tightened uploader IAM roles recently but legacy agents might still be running.
jordan.lee: immediate mitigation ideas?
mike.carter: block further legacy uploads by enforcing an IAM condition on uploader role that requires request tag `retention-level` and `kms:EncryptionContext/tenant_id`. That prevents new untagged uploads.
sarah.nelson: for detection: add CloudTrail rule to capture PutObjectTagging, PutObjectAcl, and CopyObject events and forward to security-audit index. We currently miss object tagging changes.
leo: re-encryption plan?
mike.carter: two paths:
- Rewrap: where object is SSE-KMS with old CMK, call KMS ReEncrypt (or S3 copy preserving metadata) to new CMK, update tag to `retention-level: archive`.
- For SSE-S3 objects: perform S3 CopyObject into same key with SSE-KMS and correct metadata/tags, or copy to a quarantine bucket and then back.
jordan.lee: perms for rewrap job: don't give the job broad kms:Decrypt. Use ephemeral grants scoped to the rewrap principal and narrow key policies, or use grant tokens and limit via kms:ViaService conditions.
sarah.nelson: tenant-safety check: some objects have `x-amz-meta-tenant` metadata. We must assert tenant->CMK mapping before rewrapping or we risk mixing tenant keys.
mike.carter: agreed. Sarah, please run a sampled heuristic: 1k objects across the two buckets, compare x-amz-meta-tenant vs tenant registry. If mismatches >0.5% escalate to legal.
sarah.nelson: on it. I'll also script a metadata inventory that flags any retention-level missing or set to none.
leo: containment script to run if we find public exposure?
mike.carter: containment steps: 1) check ACLs and block public access (s3api get-object-acl/get-bucket-policy). 2) remove public ACLs and revoke any pre-signed URLs. 3) apply restrictive bucket policy denying GetObject unless kms:EncryptionContext tenant matches and principal is our service.
jordan.lee: add to that: revoke any long-lived uploader credentials that might have been used, and rotate them after rewrap job.
sarah.nelson: cloudtrail rule: PutObjectTagging/PutObjectAcl/CopyObject => security-audit. Also add a detection rule: any PutObject where x-amz-server-side-encryption = AES256 (SSE-S3) triggers review.
leo: timeline for fixes?
mike.carter: short plan:
- Today: detection + sample (Sarah)
- 24h: IAM condition PR to block legacy uploads (Jordan)
- 48-72h: rewrap job design + perms + pilot (Jordan + Mike)
- Containment script ready in parallel (Leo)
- Only escalate to customers/legal if sample finds PII or confirmed public exposure.
jordan.lee: note from infra: rewrapping 3k objects will cause KMS requests surge. Request KMS quota bump or use batched windows to avoid throttle.
sarah.nelson: also add audit trail of all rewrap copy events: log original etag, new etag, object key, tenant meta, and store bundle in secure archive.
mike.carter: good. Also add test coverage: agent upload path should fail if required tags not present. Jordan, include integration tests.
leo: SRE bot note?
sre-bot: Reminder: IAM policy deploys require on-call approval if done during deploy window 02:00-04:00 UTC. Schedule changes accordingly.
mike.carter: thanks. Assignments: Sarah -> sample + detection PR; Jordan -> IAM condition change + rewrap perms; Leo -> containment scripts and runbook. I'll coordinate incident channel if we escalate.
sarah.nelson: starting the sample run now, will post results in this thread when ready.
leo: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
